To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the power consumption of serial elastic actuators is dominated by the mechanical friction, (2) the energy consumption can be reduced by 30% by exploiting the natural dynamics of the system, (3) the stiffness control can be implemented without any model of the system, and (4) the control is robust to changes in friction and electrical dynamics.
stiffness control of a variable elastic actuator with serial elasticity is possible by exploiting its natural dynamics, and that this yields a significant reduction of power and energy consumption.
the energy efficiency of variable stiffness actuations with serial elasticity can be significantly increased through stiffness control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new type of energy-efficient variable stiffness actuator.
a better understanding of the mechanical dynamics of variable elastic actuators, the development of an efficient stiffness control method and the experimental validation of the approach.
the development of a novel actuator concept for physical human–robot interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the exploitation of the natural dynamics of variable serial elastic actuators is a promising strategy for the energy efficiency of such systems.
a variable stiffness actuator with serial elasticity is a good choice if the actuator is not operated in resonance.
the exploitation of natural dynamics is a very promising approach for energy efficient control of variable stiffness actuactors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a variable serial elastic actuator is a very promising solution for energy efficient and safe physical human–robot interactions.
the exploitation of the natural behavior of variable stiffness actuations can be used to improve energy efficiency.
stiffness control of a serially elastic actuator should be based on the natural mechanical dynamics of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy efficiency of a serially elastic actuator can be increased by exploiting the natural dynamics.
the energy efficiency of variable serial elastic actuators is strongly influenced by the natural dynamics of the system.
stiffness control of elastic actuation systems is a promising strategy for energy efficiency.
